title.value: Characterizing User Behaviors in Open-Source Software User Forums: An Empirical Study
title.justification: The title provided is from the paper itself, directly indicating the study focus.
title.quote: Characterizing User Behaviors in Open-Source Software User Forums: An Empirical Study

extractions.description: The paper investigates user behaviors in user forums of Open Source Software (OSS), focusing on how end-users engage, participate, and communicate in such forums. An empirical analysis of about 1.3 million posts from forums related to Zotero, Audacity, VLC, and RStudio was conducted. It explores the roles of end-users, developers, and organizers based on their contributions and the linguistic analysis of their interactions, aiming to improve end-user engagement in OSS development.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on user behaviors in OSS forums, which is more related to software engineering and community management than climate or ecological sustainability.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: User forums of Open Source Software (OSS) enable end-users to collaboratively discuss problems concerning the OSS applications.

primary_category.justification: The study centers on software engineering and user engagement in software forums, without direct linkages to climate or ecological sustainable development.
primary_category.quote: Despite decades of research on OSS, we know very little about how end-users engage with OSS communities on these forums...

secondary_categories.justification: The scope of the paper does not extend to any specific element within climate or ecological sustainable development but remains within the realm of software and community studies.
secondary_categories.quote: Many previous works are developer-centric and overlook the importance of end-user forums.

primary_sub_category.justification: The subject matter does not align directly with any sub-category in climate or ecological sustainable development.
primary_sub_category.quote: Forums are a communication channel for OSS communities...

secondary_sub_categories.justification: There is no clear fit for the work in the sub-categories outlined for climate or ecological development.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Our work contributes new knowledge about end-users’ activities and behaviors in OSS user forums...

applications.justification: The paper does not discuss applications relevant to climate or ecological sustainable development but focuses on OSS user interactions and engagement.
applications.quote: end-users not only initiated most of the threads but also acted as the significant contributors for responding to other users’ posts...

new_primary_category.justification: As the focus of the study is on OSS user forum engagement and not on a topic related to climate or ecological sustainability, there is no need to suggest a new sustainability category.
new_primary_category.quote: To better understand user behaviors in OSS user fo-rums, we carried out an empirical study analyzing about 1.3 million posts...

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The existing sub-categories do not encompass user engagement in OSS forums sufficiently to warrant a new sub-category under sustainability categories.
